posts.title: How to order a motion graphics video: from storyboard to final animation
posts.metaTitle: How to order a motion video and storyboard | ChikChirik
posts.metaDesc: Stages of a motion video: brief, script, storyboard, style frames, animatic, animation. What to approve at each step and how to order a storyboard alone.
posts.lead: A motion video is made step by step: script and storyboard first, then style, animatic and only at the end — animation. Here's what happens at each stage, what you approve and why a change at the storyboard stage costs less than a change to a finished video.

ps: To get a video without endless revisions, approve the work stage by stage: script → storyboard → style frames → animatic → animation → sound. The earlier a mistake is caught, the cheaper it is to fix: changing a frame in a storyboard takes minutes, redoing finished animation takes days.

head: Stage
What the designer does
What you approve
rows: Studies the task and asks questions
Goal, length, format, deadline and budget
Writes the text and voice-over, splits the video into scenes
Message and text — later changes mean re-estimating
Draws key frames for each scene with captions
Composition, scene order and what happens in frame
Makes 2–3 frames in the final style
Colours, fonts, characters and overall look
Assembles the storyboard into a rough video with timing and voice
Motion details — revisions within what's approved
Adds music and effects, exports formats

sections.h: What a storyboard is and why order one
ps: A storyboard is the video drawn frame by frame, like a comic: under each frame is what happens, the text and the approximate duration. It shows the whole video before expensive animation begins.

You can order a storyboard on its own — for example, to agree on the idea inside your company, get quotes from several studios or hand it to another animator. It's usually needed for explainer videos, ads and character animation; for a short logo animation a single style frame is often enough.

sections.h: What to prepare before you start
items: The goal of the video and where it will be shown: reels, website, presentation, TV.
Length and format: vertical 9:16, square 1:1 or horizontal 16:9.
The text or key points.
Logo in vector format, brand colours and fonts.
3–5 reference videos you like — and what exactly you like about them.
Whether you need a voice-over and in which languages.
Deadline and budget.

sections.h: 2D, 3D or AI: which format to choose
ps: 2D animation is the most common choice for explainers, infographics and logo animation. 3D is needed when you want to show a product from every angle or complex equipment — it takes longer and costs more to produce. AI tools help make backgrounds, concepts or short scenes quickly, but it's harder to control every frame, so for a precise brand video they're usually combined with classic animation.

sections.h: What to ask a motion designer
items: Show me your showreel and 2–3 projects in a similar style.
Do you write the script and storyboard yourself, or work with mine?
How many rounds of revisions are included at each stage?
Will there be an animatic before the final animation?
Who handles voice-over and music, and are the music rights covered?
Which formats will I receive, and do I get the source files?

ps: The designer sets the price, and you state your budget in the task. The biggest factors are length, style (2D or 3D, characters or graphics), the number of scenes, whether you need a script, storyboard and voice-over, and the deadline. For market benchmarks, see our article on creative service prices.

sections.h: How to find a motion designer on ChikChirik
ps: Describe the task in the app: what kind of video, its length and format, whether you need a storyboard, and the deadline. Motion designers will reply with showreels — compare them using the questions above. If you only need a storyboard, say so in the task.

links.text: How to write a brief for a videographer

faq.q: What are the stages of making a motion video?
faq.a: Usually six: brief and script, storyboard, style frames, animatic, animation, sound and delivery. For short videos some stages are combined.

faq.q: Can I order just an animation storyboard?
faq.a: Yes. Storyboards are ordered separately to agree on the idea, estimate the budget or hand over to an animator. Say in the task that you only need a storyboard and roughly how many scenes there will be.

faq.q: How is a storyboard different from an animatic?
faq.a: A storyboard is static frames with captions. An animatic is the same frames assembled into a video with timing and voice — it shows the pace of the video.

faq.q: How many revisions are usually included?
faq.a: It's agreed with the designer. A common practice is a few rounds of revisions at each stage, with changes after a stage is approved charged separately. Agree on the terms in the chat before you start.

posts.title: Mobile videographer or videographer: who to hire for reels
posts.metaTitle: Mobile videographer or videographer: who to hire | ChikChirik
posts.metaDesc: How a mobile videographer differs from a videographer, who to book for reels, ads or events, and what to ask before the shoot. Tasks, gear and results compared.
posts.lead: A mobile videographer shoots on a smartphone; a videographer works with a camera, lighting and sound. Both make video for social media, but for different jobs. Here's how they differ, who to pick for reels, ads or events, and what to agree on before the shoot.

ps: Need regular content for Instagram and TikTok — reels, stories, unboxings — go with a mobile videographer. Need an ad, a music video, an interview or event coverage with clean sound — hire a videographer. If you're not sure, start with one question: where will the video live, and how many clips do you need a month?

head: Mobile videographer
Videographer
rows: Smartphone, gimbal, compact light and a lav mic
Camera, interchangeable lenses, lighting, separate audio recording
Ads, music videos, interviews, company films, events
Shoots and edits fast, often on the same day
More time for prep, shooting and editing
Video where image, sound and staging matter

sections.h: When you need a mobile videographer
items: You run Instagram or TikTok and need content every week.
You're filming a café, salon, shop or showroom as it is, without heavy staging.
You need unboxings, product reviews, behind-the-scenes and trends.
You want clips fast — on the day of the shoot or the next day.
You want to shoot regularly: several sessions a month.
An ad for paid social, TV or your website.
An interview, podcast or expert video where clean sound matters.
A wedding, conference, concert or another event.
A music video, brand film or company film.
A horizontal version for YouTube or a screen at an event.

ps: Yes, and it's a common setup. A videographer shoots the main video once a quarter, and a mobile videographer keeps the account going in between. Another option is to ask the videographer to cut vertical versions for reels — many do, but it's extra work, so agree on it upfront.
The line between the two is blurry: some videographers shoot reels, and some mobile videographers work with a camera. Look at the portfolio in the format you need, not at the job title.

sections.h: How to prepare for the shoot
items: Set the goal: reach, leads or awareness — it shapes the format of the clips.
Collect 3–5 example videos you like and show them to the creator.
Prepare the location: light, a clean background, the product or dishes in frame.
Let staff and guests know about the shoot and decide who will be on camera.
Agree on how you'll receive the files and whether you need the raw footage.

sections.h: What to ask before the shoot
ps: These questions work for both:
items: Show me 3–5 projects in my niche and in the format I need.
How many clips will one shoot produce, and how long are they?
Who comes up with the scripts and ideas?
Are editing, music, subtitles and color grading included?
How many revisions are included, and when will it be ready?
Do we need lighting, a mic or an assistant on set?

ps: The creator sets the price, and you state your budget in the task. The cost depends on the number of clips, the script, editing, gear, travel and shooting time. We've collected market benchmarks in a separate article on creative service prices.

sections.h: How to find a creator on ChikChirik
ps: Describe the task in the app: what to film, for which platform, how many clips and by when. Mobile videographers and videographers will reply with examples of their work — then compare them using the questions above. Writing a brief for the first time? Use our template.

links.text: How to write a brief for a videographer

faq.q: Mobile videographer or videographer — who should shoot my reels?
faq.a: For regular reels and stories, a mobile videographer is usually enough: they shoot fast and straight in vertical format. Hire a videographer when it's an ad and lighting, sound and staging matter.

faq.q: How is a mobile videographer different from a videographer?
faq.a: A mobile videographer shoots on a smartphone and makes short content for social media. A videographer works with a camera, lighting and sound and makes ads, music videos, interviews and event coverage.

faq.q: Do I need a script to shoot reels?
faq.a: It helps. Even a short plan — what to show, what to say and the call to action — saves time on set. Many mobile videographers help with scripts, so ask in the chat.

faq.q: Can a videographer shoot reels too?
faq.a: Yes, many videographers cut vertical versions from the main shoot. Agree on it upfront: it's extra editing and may affect the price and timeline.

posts.title: SMM specialist or targeting specialist: who to hire for your business
posts.metaTitle: SMM specialist or targeting specialist: who to hire | ChikChirik
posts.metaDesc: How an SMM specialist differs from a targeting specialist, who to hire for your task and whether one person can do both. A comparison of tasks, results and pay.
posts.lead: An SMM specialist and a targeting specialist often work in the same account but are responsible for different things: the first for content and the audience, the second for paid ads. Here is how they differ, who to hire for your task and when you need both.

ps: If you need the account run regularly and content made, hire an SMM specialist. If you need leads and sales from paid ads, hire a targeting specialist. If the account is empty, start with SMM: there's nowhere to send ad traffic until the profile has content.

head: SMM specialist
Targeting specialist
rows: Run the account and build relationships with the audience
Bring leads and sales through paid ads
Content plan, posts, reels, stories, replies to followers
Set up ad campaigns, audiences and creatives, run tests
An active account, reach, engagement, awareness
Leads, clicks, sales, cost per lead
Gradually, over several months of regular work
Faster — from the first days of the campaign
Campaign setup and management; the ad budget is separate

sections.h: When you need an SMM specialist
items: The account is empty or updated irregularly.
You need a consistent style and a content plan a month ahead.
Replying to followers and building a community matters.
The brand is just launching and needs awareness.

sections.h: When you need a targeting specialist
items: The account already has content, reviews and a clear offer.
You need leads or sales soon.
You have an ad budget and are ready to test.
You need to promote a sale, a launch or a specific product.

ps: Many SMM specialists can set up ads, and targeting specialists can make simple content. For a small business this is often sensible: one contractor, one point of responsibility.
If ads are your main source of sales and the budget is large, a separate specialist with deep knowledge of ad accounts is better.
These questions help compare candidates in their responses:
items: SMM: show the accounts you run and the results over several months.
SMM: how many posts a month are included and who shoots the content?
SMM: how do you report and what do you count as success?
Targeting: show case studies with cost per lead and ad budget.
Targeting: how will you test audiences and creatives?
Targeting: how will you access the ad account — through roles, without my password?

sections.h: How to find a specialist on ChikChirik
ps: Describe your task in the app: your niche, social networks, goal — awareness or leads — and budget. SMM and targeting specialists will send responses with case studies; then compare them using the questions from this article.

faq.q: How is SMM different from targeted ads?
faq.a: SMM is social media management and content; targeted ads are paid advertising aimed at a specific audience. SMM builds awareness and trust, targeted ads bring leads and sales.

faq.q: Who should I hire first: an SMM specialist or a targeting specialist?
faq.a: If the account is empty, an SMM specialist: you need content first that ads can lead to. If the account is set up and you need sales, a targeting specialist.

faq.q: Is the ad budget included in the targeting specialist's fee?
faq.a: Usually not: payment for the work and the ad budget are separate. Check this in advance and put it in writing.

faq.q: Can one specialist do both SMM and targeted ads?
faq.a: Yes, many specialists do both. It's convenient for a small business; with a large ad budget a separate targeting specialist is better.

posts.title: How to choose a photographer: portfolio, questions and agreements
posts.metaTitle: How to choose a photographer: a client checklist | ChikChirik
posts.metaDesc: How to choose a photographer for a photo shoot, business or event: what to look for in a portfolio, which questions to ask and what to agree on before the shoot.
posts.lead: There are plenty of photographers, but not all of them will shoot your task well. Here is a step-by-step guide: which genre you need, how to read a portfolio, what to ask before the shoot and what to put in writing — so you get the photos you need on time and without disputes.

ps: Choose a photographer for the genre of your task, look at full series rather than just the best shots, agree on the number of photos, retouching, deadlines and usage rights in advance — and put it all in writing.
Photographers specialise: a good wedding photographer won't necessarily shoot product photos for a marketplace. First work out which genre you need — that decides whose portfolio to look at.

head: Task
Genre
What to look for in the portfolio
rows: Photos for Kaspi, a website or a marketplace
Clean background, accurate colours, consistent light across the product series
Natural faces, careful retouching, different types of people
Candid moments, low-light shooting, many shots from one event
Working with people and posing, editing style
Appetising presentation, straight lines, indoor lighting
Working with models, one style across the series

items: Look for 3–5 works in your genre — beautiful weddings don't guarantee good product shots.
Ask for a full series from one shoot: it shows the quality of every shot, not just the best ones.
Check consistency: light, colour and editing should be even across the whole series.
Read the reviews in the profile and note what clients praise and complain about.

sections.h: Step 3. Ask questions before the shoot
ps: The answers will show right away whether your expectations match:
items: How many photos will I get and how many will be retouched?
When will the photos be ready?
Do you have your own lighting and studio, or do I pay for the rental?
How long is the shoot and what happens if it runs over?
How many editing revisions are included in the price?
Where and how can I use the photos — is advertising allowed?

sections.h: Step 4. Put the agreements in writing
ps: Even if you agreed on everything by phone, repeat the terms in a message. It protects both sides and prevents disputes after the shoot.
items: Date, time, location and length of the shoot.
Number of photos, format and depth of retouching.
Delivery deadline and number of revisions.
The price, what it includes and how payment works.
Don't pay the full amount before the shoot: it's sensible to pay part in advance and the rest after you receive the photos.
The portfolio has no work in your genre.
The photographer can't name the deadline or the number of photos.
They demand full prepayment and avoid written agreements.
The price is noticeably lower than others' with no explanation.

sections.h: How to find a photographer on ChikChirik
ps: Describe your task in the app: genre, city, date, how many photos you need and your budget. Photographers will send responses with their portfolios — then compare the work and ask the questions from this article in the chat.

faq.q: How do I choose a photographer for a photo shoot?
faq.a: Look at portfolios with portrait shoots specifically, ask for a full series from one shoot and agree on the look, location, number of photos and deadlines in advance.

faq.q: What should I ask a photographer before the shoot?
faq.a: How many photos there will be and how many retouched, when they will be delivered, who pays for the studio, how many revisions are included and whether the photos can be used in advertising.

faq.q: Do I need a contract with a photographer?
faq.a: For a large or commercial shoot, a contract is better. For a small one, at least put the terms in writing in your messages.

faq.q: How much does a photographer cost?
faq.a: It depends on the genre, the length of the shoot, retouching and studio rental. See our article on creative service prices for reference figures.

posts.title: How much videographers, photographers, editors and SMM cost in Kazakhstan in 2026

posts.metaDesc: What videographers, mobile videographers, photographers, video editors and SMM cost in Almaty and Astana: price ranges as of October 2026 and what drives them.
posts.lead: Prices for creative services in Kazakhstan vary tenfold: one videographer in the classifieds charges ₸10,000, another ₸450,000. We collected public price lists from platforms, classifieds and agencies as of October 2026 to show the real ranges and explain what the price is made of.

ps: Below are ranges for Almaty and Astana. The lower end is beginners and simple tasks, the upper end is experienced professionals and production-level work. Most orders land in the middle.

head: Specialist
Priced by
Range, ₸
rows: Social media management by an agency

notes: Sources: Profi.kz price lists (Almaty and Astana), Kaspi Obyavleniya and OLX listings, studio and SMM agency websites — as of October 2026. Ad budget, studio rental and out-of-town travel are not included.

ps: Hourly rates for camera operators on Profi.kz in Almaty range from ₸5,000 to ₸100,000. Experienced videographers usually quote ₸15,000–50,000 per hour of filming. A studio may charge about ₸35,000 per hour without editing, and an agency shift of 4–8 hours starts at ₸139,200.

Kaspi listings more often offer packages: a reels shoot with simple editing costs ₸15,000–35,000, a turnkey ad or event video ₸30,000 to ₸450,000. Mobile videographers on Profi.kz charge ₸10,000–40,000 per hour.
Always check whether editing is included: it is often a separate line.

Portrait, commercial and content photography in Almaty costs ₸15,000–50,000 per hour, product photography ₸12,000–35,000 per hour, food photography ₸10,000–30,000. Retouching is priced separately: ₸500 to ₸10,000 per photo depending on complexity.
If you need a studio, rental adds from ₸8,000 per hour.

Editing one reel costs from ₸3,500 with beginner editors. On Profi.kz in Almaty the range is ₸5,000–48,000 per video. Length, color grading, graphics, subtitles and the number of revisions push the price up.
One-off SMM services on Profi.kz start at ₸8,000, Instagram promotion costs ₸16,000–100,000, targeted ad setup ₸20,000–120,000. The ad budget is paid separately.

Social media management by an agency in Almaty starts at ₸139,000 per month; full packages with content and ads cost ₸350,000–700,000. Freelancers usually charge less than agencies, but compare the scope: posts, reels, stories, filming, reports.

Simple tasks — a banner, a cover, a post — start at ₸2,800 on Profi.kz, simple animation from motion designers at ₸2,490. A logo, brand identity or complex animation is quoted per project: ask for an estimate with stages and the number of options.

Kwork, Freelancehunt, allfreelance.kz and similar exchanges are handy for remote tasks: design, editing, motion. Downsides: most are not Kazakh, there are few creators for shoots in Almaty and Astana, and safe-deal payments usually carry a commission. Good if location doesn't matter.
Not for one-off projects but for full-time hiring or long contracts: you post a vacancy or search CVs. If you need a videographer or SMM manager on staff, this is the place.

posts.title: How to write a brief for a videographer: template and example
posts.metaTitle: Videographer brief: template and example | ChikChirik
posts.metaDesc: How to write a brief for a videographer: goal, format, timing and budget. A ready-to-use template, a filled-in example and common mistakes.
posts.lead: A good brief saves time and money: the videographer understands the task right away, quotes an accurate price and doesn’t spend days on questions. Here’s what to include in a brief, plus a ready template you can copy and paste into your task on ChikChirik.

ps: Without a brief, a videographer answers “it depends” and guesses the price. With a brief, they immediately see the scope, the equipment needed and the timeline. You get accurate responses and compare offers on the same terms.
A brief doesn’t have to be long. Answering the eight questions below takes 10–15 minutes.

sections.h: What to include in a brief
items: Goal of the video. What it’s for: sales, awareness, a product presentation, an event recap.
Where the video will be used. Instagram and TikTok — vertical 9:16, YouTube and websites — horizontal 16:9, ads or a screen at an event.
Format and length. For example: 3 reels of 30 seconds or one 1–2 minute video.
What and where to film. Location, people on camera, a product or a process. Whether a studio is needed.
Shoot date and time. The exact day and how many hours the shoot will take.
Editing and deliverables. Whether you need editing, colour grading, music, subtitles, how many rounds of revisions and whether you need the raw footage.
References. 2–3 videos whose style you like — clearer than any description.
Budget and deadline. Your budget range and the date you need the finished video.

ps: Copy the template, fill it in and paste it into your task description on ChikChirik — videographers will see all the details at once.

example: Goal of the video: attract guests to a new coffee shop.
Where it will be published: Instagram and TikTok.
Format and length: 4 vertical reels of 20–30 seconds.
What we film: the interior, coffee being made, baristas and guests.
Location and shoot date: a coffee shop in Almaty, Saturday, 10:00–13:00.
Editing and deliverables: edited with music and subtitles, 2 rounds of revisions.
References (links): 2 reels from other coffee shops.

items: No goal — the videographer films something “beautiful” but not what you need for sales.
No format — the video was shot horizontally when you needed vertical reels.
No references — you and the videographer imagine different styles.
Revisions not discussed — every change turns into an argument.
No budget — you get responses with prices far from what you expected.

sections.h: How to find a videographer on ChikChirik
ps: Download the app, describe your task using the template and state your budget. Videographers will send responses with portfolios — compare their work and agree on the details in chat.
Posting a task and receiving responses is free.

links.text: Where to hire a videographer: 6 platforms

faq.q: How long does it take to write a brief?
faq.a: 10–15 minutes if you answer the questions in the template. That’s enough to get accurate responses.

faq.q: What if I don’t know which format I need?
faq.a: Say where the video will be published and the videographer will suggest the format. Reels and TikTok usually need a vertical 9:16 video.

faq.q: Do I need a brief for a simple shoot?
faq.a: Yes, even a short one: goal, format, date and budget. A few lines prevent misunderstandings.

faq.q: Can I change the brief after work starts?
faq.a: You can, but discuss it with the videographer first: changes may affect the timeline and the price.
